data.translation:
Age 23 means you're still in college, right? Try checking out Coursera.

So, take courses that match your major. For example, if it's business, go for
- Business Foundations by Wharton
- Financial Markets by Yale
If you're a software engineer, you can take
- Front-End Developer by Meta
- Algorithms by Stanford
This is just an example, okay..

You can filter by university, major, or other skills.

Some courses on Coursera can be accessed for free without a certificate, at least preview the first module. But if you want the full thing + certification, you can get a subscription

I subscribed for a year, you really need to be consistent :')
I'm not very consistent lololol, it's cheaper to pay 200k per month for a year (during promo)
Worth it!

Besides that, you can also take skills for job prep, critical thinking is needed too
- Leadership by University of Michigan (Inspiring and Motivating Individuals)
- AI skills by DeepLearningAI (AI For Everyone)
- Prompting skills by Vanderbilt (Prompt Engineering for ChatGPT)
- How to use Excel by Macquarie University (Excel Skills for Business)
- Critical thinking by Duke (Introduction to Logic and Critical Thinking)
- Communication by Wharton (Improving Communication Skills)
Etc

So yeah, check if Coursera is worth it too. So your choices can be spot on, right
